gap: No result ChatGPT got states that only three TMR boards sit at or under $100 at their makers' US stores on 2026-11-26 (Epomaker HE65 V2 TMR $59.99, MonsGeek FUN60 Ultra TMR $79.99-$89.99, Gamakay TK75 TMR $89.99 on sale), which makes the Gamakay the only 75% one, while the 75% board ChatGPT showed at $85.99 (Womier K75 TMR) is $119.99 at Womier's own store.
standout_why: Compared against mkbguide (prints no prices at all), keyboardtester.click (TK75 TMR at $109.99 on Nov 5, so over the line; no HE65 V2 TMR or K75 TMR), hlplanet and the apidog page (TK75 TMR at $114.99; apidog names the FUN60 Ultra as the only TMR board under $100), gamepadsquire (FUN60 Ultra TMR is its only TMR board) and PCWorld (FUN60 only, a $74.99 price widget). None has all three under-$100 boards priced on one date, none shows the TK75 TMR under $100, and none prices the Womier K75 TMR. The RTINGS pages returned only navigation, so they are not compared.
decides: It does not change the overall pick: the Epomaker HE65 V2 TMR at $59.99 is the lowest-priced TMR board read, and the FUN60 Ultra TMR is the 60% alternative at $79.99-$89.99. It does change the 'larger layout' slot: ChatGPT's Womier K75 TMR is over budget at its maker's store, and the Gamakay TK75 TMR (ours) is the only 75% TMR board under $100 at a maker store read today, at its Black Friday price only (list $159.99). So ours honestly wins the 75% / function-row segment and places in the top three, because only three boards qualify.
